# [CS077] Request Built for Plaintext HTTP (go.security.plaintext-http-request-new)

http.NewRequestWithContext is called with a constant http:// URL of a host other than localhost.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | MEDIUM |
| **Category** | Security |
| **CWE** | [CWE-319](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/319.html) |
| **OWASP** | A04:2025 |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

A request built for a plain HTTP URL travels unencrypted, so headers such as Authorization and the body can be read and changed in transit. Like go.security.plaintext-http-request, only constant URLs are matched and local hosts are allowed.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodPost, "http://billing.example.com/charge", body)
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodPost, "https://billing.example.com/charge", body)
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [go.security.plaintext-http-request-new]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    go.security.plaintext-http-request-new: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore go.security.plaintext-http-request-new -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** go.security.plaintext-http-request-new
```
